about.heading: A Marketer Who Understands Both Strategy and Execution
paragraphs: I'm Muhammad Awais Rustam Malik, a Marketing Specialist working in Qatar. I started my career in digital marketing in 2019, and since then my work has sat where strategy meets day-to-day execution: planning campaigns, running paid advertising, producing the creative and following through on the leads it brings in.

Today I work at Target Trading and Contracting, within the Target business structure that includes Target Furniture Factory and Target Metal Forming. I joined as Digital Marketing Executive and moved into my current role as Marketing Specialist, supporting marketing for furniture, wood-related and stainless steel products.

Before that I was Digital Marketing Manager at Leaders Training Center from June 2024 to May 2025, where I looked after SEO, Google Ads, social media, lead generation, content, design, video, email and WhatsApp broadcasts, and the marketing budget.
My approach is simple: understand what the business needs, reach the people who matter, communicate clearly, and judge the work by outcomes rather than clicks.

guide.heading: Digital marketing, answered
guide.intro: Short, straight answers to the questions business owners in Qatar ask most, based on the campaigns I work on.

items.a: Digital marketing is promoting a business through online channels, such as Google search, social media, email, WhatsApp and websites, to reach buyers, generate leads and drive sales that can be measured.
points: Paid channels: Google Ads, Meta Ads (Facebook and Instagram), TikTok and LinkedIn ads.
Owned channels: your website, SEO content, email lists and WhatsApp Business.
Every campaign is tracked by numbers such as cost per lead (CPL), return on ad spend (ROAS) and lead-to-sale ratio.

items.q: Which digital marketing channels work best in Qatar?
items.a: For most businesses in Qatar, Meta Ads (Instagram and Facebook) and Google Ads bring the most leads, with WhatsApp as the main follow-up channel. B2B companies also benefit from Google Search and LinkedIn.
points: Instagram and Facebook lead forms work well for training, retail, real estate and services.
Google Search captures buyers who are already looking, which suits B2B and high-value services.
Fast WhatsApp follow-up is what turns a lead into a sale in the Gulf market.
Plan seasonal campaigns for Ramadan, Eid and Qatar National Day early.

items.q: How much should I spend on Meta and Google Ads?
items.a: Set your ad budget from your lead target: multiply the number of leads you need each month by your target cost per lead, then split it between channels based on where your buyers search and scroll.
points: Example: at Leaders Training Center I managed lead-generation budgets of QAR 45,000 on social media and QAR 15,000 on Google Ads.
Start with a test budget for two to four weeks, then move spend to the ads with the lowest cost per qualified lead.
Judge results by qualified leads and sales, not clicks or likes.

items.q: What is the difference between SEO, AEO and GEO?
items.a: SEO helps your website rank in Google’s results, AEO (answer engine optimisation) helps your content become the direct answer in featured snippets and voice search, and GEO (generative engine optimisation) helps AI tools like ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity mention and cite your brand.
points: SEO: keywords, fast pages, helpful content and links from other websites.
AEO: question-led headings, one-sentence answers and FAQ structured data.
GEO: clear facts about who you are, consistent profiles across the web, and content AI tools can read and quote.

items.q: Which digital marketing trends matter most right now?
items.a: The trends that move results today are AI search visibility, AI-assisted creative testing, short-form video, WhatsApp conversations, and first-party data with privacy-safe tracking.
points: Buyers now ask AI assistants for recommendations, so brands need AEO and GEO, not only SEO.
Testing many ad creatives quickly, with AI helping on variations, keeps cost per lead down.
Reels and TikTok-style video reach the most people per riyal on social.
Conversions API and Google consent mode keep ad tracking accurate as cookies disappear.

items.q: How do I know if my digital marketing is working?
items.a: Digital marketing is working when cost per qualified lead falls and the share of leads that become customers rises. Track CPL, lead-to-sale ratio and return on ad spend every week, not just clicks and likes.
points: CTR and CPC show if the ad gets attention.
CPL and lead quality show if the offer and targeting are right.
Lead-to-sale ratio and ROAS show if marketing is making money.

items.q: Should I hire a digital marketing specialist or an agency?
items.a: Hire a specialist when you want one senior person who plans, runs and designs your campaigns and reports directly to you; choose an agency when you need a large team across many services at once.
points: A specialist usually costs less and moves faster because strategy, ads and creative sit with one person.
Ask any candidate how they measured past campaigns, and which results are verified.

items.title: Digital marketing and B2B lead generation for Target Furniture Factory
items.summary: Bringing relevant B2B enquiries to a furniture and wood-products business in Qatar through Meta advertising, clear product communication and careful audience targeting.
items.objective: Generate relevant enquiries from businesses and project buyers for furniture, wood panels and related products, while building awareness of the brand in Qatar.
items.challenge: The buyers are contractors, fit-out companies, interior designers and businesses, not general consumers. Reaching that small professional audience on social platforms, and telling a genuinely interested prospect apart from a casual click, needs careful targeting and honest lead assessment.
responsibilities: Planning and running Meta advertising for the wood division
Marketing graphics and social media content
Enquiry generation and lead quality assessment
approach: Built campaigns around specific product lines, such as wood panels and furniture, rather than one generic message.
Targeted business and project audiences, then refined targeting as enquiry quality became clearer.
Designed product-focused creatives that explain the product and its use in a fit-out.
Reviewed enquiries for relevance, project timing and product interest, not only volume.
items.lessons: In B2B, a prospect who is not ready to buy this month can still be a strong lead. Project timing and genuine product interest matter as much as speed to purchase.

items.title: Managing digital marketing for Leaders Training Center
items.summary: Running the full digital marketing function for a training business, from SEO and Google Ads to social media, content, video and lead generation.
items.objective: Generate enquiries for a wide range of courses and keep the brand visible across search and social channels.
items.challenge: Many different courses, each with its own audience, competing for one marketing budget, with every channel needing to be planned, produced and followed up.
approach: Split lead-generation budgets between social media and Google Ads according to where each audience searches and scrolls.
Produced course creatives, video content and social posts in-house.
Followed up enquiries through email and WhatsApp broadcasts.
Reviewed campaign performance and moved budget toward what worked.
items.lessons: Owning every channel at once makes consistency easier: the same message runs through the ad, the creative and the follow-up.

items.title: Google Ads and search marketing
items.summary: How I structure search campaigns: keyword intent, campaign structure, conversion tracking and ongoing optimisation.
items.objective: Reach people who are already searching for a product or service, and turn that intent into relevant enquiries.
items.challenge: Search budgets are easy to waste on broad or irrelevant keywords, and results are only as reliable as the conversion tracking behind them.
approach: Group keywords by intent so each ad group answers one kind of search.
Use negative keywords to keep spend on relevant searches.
Set up conversion tracking before scaling budget.
Review search terms and adjust bids and ads regularly.
items.lessons: Editable draft: campaign screenshots and verified results will be added here.

items.title: Creative and brand communication
items.summary: Marketing graphics, social media creatives and promotional campaigns for brands across furniture, retail, real estate, food and training.
items.objective: Give each brand a clear, consistent visual voice that supports its campaigns.
items.challenge: Very different industries, from industrial B2B products to restaurants and real estate, each needing its own look while staying on-brand.
approach: Start from the campaign message, then design the visual around it.
Keep a consistent look per brand across posts, covers and ads.
Adapt each design for the format it will run in.
items.lessons: Good creative starts with a clear message; the design is how that message gets noticed.

approach.heading: Understand, Plan, Execute, Measure, Improve
approach.intro: Effective marketing is not only about generating clicks or collecting enquiries. It starts with the business objective, reaches relevant audiences, communicates value clearly, measures outcomes that matter, and improves based on evidence.

steps.title: Understand
steps.text: Start with the business objective, the product and who actually buys it, before choosing a channel.

steps.title: Plan
steps.text: Set the audience, message, channels and budget around that objective, with clear measures of success.

steps.title: Execute
steps.text: Build the campaigns, produce the creative and keep communication consistent across every touchpoint.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Look past clicks to enquiry quality, follow-up and the outcomes the business cares about.

steps.title: Improve
steps.text: Adjust targeting, creative and budget based on evidence, then repeat.

approach.note: A B2B prospect is not automatically a poor lead just because they are not ready to buy today. Relevance, project timing, product interest and genuine buying signals matter too. A contractor planning a fit-out six months from now can be one of the most valuable enquiries a campaign brings in, as long as the follow-up keeps the conversation alive.
